stage1.impression: A red acrylic trough glowing hot pink against dark, red-washed timber boards. Up close it reads as a render: the basin floor is visibly faceted, the under-glow is a near-white slab that clips and turns the Ember red to candy pink, and the timber is a smooth procedural with no pool of light on it. As it stands this is a generic neon display-case sink, not a specific place a design magazine would publish; it reads as signage or a nightclub vanity, not Kuramata-grade acrylic.

blocking_9: The basin's inner surface is smooth, with no faceting visible at 1:1 (region 150-310 x 215-300)
The under-glow is not seen as an object: no near-white slab, and the acrylic body reads deep Ember red, not pink (region 80-590 x 300-430: lum_median about 90 or less, clip_pct under 0.5)
Frame clip_pct under 0.5 % (now 0.84 %, all from the sink, which is not a lamp)
A real pool of 2700 K light falls from the spout onto the trough and fades up the boards, so the wall is not flat (y-profile over 220-600 x 0-200 is now 35 to 38, dead flat)
The left edge holds some timber detail instead of a black band (0-60 x 0-480: crush_pct 78)
A sign of life on the sink: a folded linen towel, a bar of soap or a small vase, so it reads as a used bar washroom
The timber shows real grain, checks and board-to-board variation instead of a smooth procedural washed in red spill
The dark object at the back-left corner (170-215 x 120-220) reads as a recognisable thing, or goes

defects.what: The basin floor is faceted into visible flat polygons and stair-steps: low tessellation or flat shading on a surface meant to be soft and rounded
The under-glow emitter shows as an opaque near-white/pink slab inside the frame, clipping (clip_pct 3.4, lum_median 148); it reads as a light box, not light passing through thick acrylic
The Ember acrylic is driven to pink (r 240 g 100 b 104 in the basin): the colour reads as neon signage, not a deep cast red
Dead black vertical band at the left edge (lum_median 1, crush_pct 78): an unlit return or the alcove edge, with nothing readable in it
The wall is lit flat (y-profile 35 to 38); there is no pool from the 28 W sink spot and nothing falls off naturally
The timber boards are a smooth procedural grain with a uniform red cast; no checks, nail holes, darker end grain or sheen variation
A dark red, unreadable object on the back-left corner of the trough (lum_median 11.6), which reads as a blob
The spout reads as a floating lever with a thin vertical pin: no escutcheon or wall plate, and it casts no shadow on the boards
The grey pad (soap rest?) is a smooth, uniform CG block with a soft plastic sheen
Thin doubled edge lines at the lower left of the frame read as coplanar or overlapping acrylic faces

changes.problem: The under-glow is visible as a clipping white slab and overdrives the acrylic to pink, which is what makes the sink read as signage.

change.to: 1.5, and the emitter hidden from camera rays (or recessed so only its light through the acrylic is seen)

changes.expected: The slab drops to a soft glow inside the acrylic, the body reads as a deep cast red with its polished edges brightest, and there is no clipping on the sink.

changes.problem: The basin's floor is faceted, so the 'soft, rounded' basin reads as low-poly CG at 1:1.

evidence.measured: Seen in a 3x crop: flat polygons and stair-stepped facets across the basin floor

change.setting: the sink basin mesh's tessellation and shading (same shape)
change.to: subdivided (2 levels or 4x the segments) with smooth shading and auto-smooth; the shape is unchanged

changes.expected: A continuous, smooth gradient across the basin, with clean refraction and no hard steps.

changes.problem: The room light has no pool: the wall is lit flat and the sink spot does not register, so nothing falls off naturally.

change.to: 60 W, cone 22 deg, aimed at the spout and the trough's rim, with the softness at 0.4

changes.expected: A warm 2700 K pool on the rim and the spout that fades up the boards: the top of the frame 15 to 25 % darker than the band just above the sink.

changes.problem: The red spill and the warm white balance together make the timber and everything else red, so the sink has no neutral to read against.

evidence.measured: Wall r/g/b median 55/23/17: a strongly red-cast 'neutral' timber

change.to: 3200 (keeping the lamps' colours), so the timber reads brown

changes.expected: The boards read as dark brown timber (g/r about 0.5 or more), and the only saturated red is the sink itself.

changes.problem: The left edge is a dead black band with no detail.

change.setting: a fill from the banquette side (or the nearest Dome downlight)
change.from: nothing reaching the alcove's left return
change.to: a 2400 K bounce of about 10 W on the left return, or reframe so the return is out of shot

changes.expected: The return holds a dim, readable edge of timber or concrete.

changes.problem: The sink is a showroom object with no sign of use.

evidence.measured: Only a featureless grey pad on the rim; no towel, soap or vessel anywhere in frame

change.to: a bar of tallow soap on the grey rest, a folded linen hand towel on the right end of the trough, and a small stoneware bud vase with one stem on the back-left corner, replacing the unreadable dark object

changes.expected: A lived-in detail with neutral props, and the trough remains the only saturated colour.

changes.problem: The timber boards are a smooth procedural, with no checks, end grain or sheen variation, which reads as CG at 1:1.

evidence.measured: In a 3x crop: uniform soft grain, p5-p95 18.5 to 39.4 across a whole board with no defects

change.to: per-board tone and stain variation of plus or minus 10 %, a roughness map of 0.35 to 0.6, fine checks and the odd nail hole, and a slightly darker board-edge reveal

changes.expected: Boards that differ from each other and show real grain under the raking spot.

changes.problem: The spout reads as a floating lever and the grey rest as a plastic block.

evidence.measured: lum_median 45.5; no shadow on the wall below the spout; the rest at 400-580 x 235-305 is uniform, median 69

change.setting: the steel's and the rest's finish
change.from: smooth glossy metal; smooth satin grey
change.to: brushed steel, anisotropic, roughness 0.3, with a wall rose; the rest in honed stone or blackened steel, roughness 0.6

changes.expected: The spout reads as brushed steel fixed to the wall, with a contact shadow, and the rest as a real material.

out_of_scope.request: Make the trough thicker-walled or give it a flush-set reveal in the boards so it reads as premium cast acrylic rather than a floating box
out_of_scope.why: The sink's design is fixed by the card; this is a design question for the owner

out_of_scope.request: Change the trough's colour from Ember red, or tint the room green to tie it to the zone
out_of_scope.why: The sink and the zone's colour are fixed

out_of_scope.request: Is this a specific place a magazine would publish? Not yet: there is nothing of Planet EARF in the frame (no concrete, fir, steel or speaker). A detail shot sells the room only if the trough is clearly the 'acrylic for special things' gesture
out_of_scope.why: Answering would mean changing the composition or the brief: widening to include the board-formed concrete or the banquette edge is a camera choice the owner should make
